int_name: S CHRISTOPHER COLUMBUS BLVD & DOCK ST

result.summary: The image shows a multi-lane urban roadway with a marked zebra crosswalk and signalized control. While sidewalks and basic crossing markings are present, the wide crossing distance across four lanes without a median refuge increases pedestrian exposure to traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross four lanes of traffic in a single stage without a mid-point refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: High Speed Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: Wide, straight travel lanes and lack of traffic calming measures encourage higher vehicle speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Main travel lanes extending into the background

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time and reduce exposure.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking or shoulder lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The image depicts an urban street with a cobblestone and brick surface, featuring wide sidewalks but lacking marked pedestrian crossings. While the textured pavement likely encourages lower vehicle speeds, the absence of formal crossing infrastructure and the presence of parked cars create potential safety and accessibility challenges.

hazards.name: Uneven Pavement Surface
hazards.description: The cobblestone roadway creates an uneven surface that can be a tripping hazard for pedestrians and difficult for those with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalks
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to designate a safe crossing point for pedestrians at this junction.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the left side of the street may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Ramps and ADA Compliance
interventions.description: Ensure the installation of detectable warning surfaces and level curb ramps at all crossing points.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.
